name: B2B Letter of Intent (LOI) Protocol
phase: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
hypothesis: We believe mid-market enterprises need our proposed integration. We will verify this by presenting a non-binding Letter of Intent (LOI) to 6 prospective enterprise accounts, and consider it validated if at least 2 authorized executives sign the document committing to a paid commercial pilot upon delivery of agreed functional specifications.
schematic: Signature at step 2 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Draft a one-page non-binding letter: the problem, the deliverables, the go-live date and pilot pricing.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Present it to the economic buyer once the requirements are defined in the sales conversation.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Note hesitation, legal and procurement redlines, and how many sign.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Draft a one-page non-binding Letter of Intent that clearly outlines the business problem, proposed deliverables, expected go-live timeline, and pilot purchase pricing terms.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Present the LOI to the economic buyer once functional requirements have been defined during enterprise sales discussions.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Note points of hesitation, redlines from legal and procurement, and final signature rates.

warning.label: Non-Binding Courtesy Signatures
warning.text: Sympathetic executives sign a non-binding letter to be kind, then vanish at procurement.

warningFull: Because standard LOIs are legally non-binding, sympathetic executives will sometimes sign them to encourage early-stage founders or wrap up exploratory calls, only to walk away when asked for formal procurement contracts and budget approvals.
